subsystems.name: Engineered organism
subsystems.role: a fast-growing marine microalga or cyanobacterium whose metabolism is rewritten to pull more carbon out of the air and water.

subsystems.name: Genetic control layer
subsystems.role: keeps the organism from spreading where it is not wanted.

subsystems.name: Growth and deployment system
subsystems.role: produces and disperses the organism at very large scale.

subsystems.name: Carbon transport and storage
subsystems.role: moves captured carbon out of contact with the atmosphere for centuries.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and verification
subsystems.role: proves how much carbon was actually removed and detects ecological side-effects.

subsystems.name: Earth-system modelling
subsystems.role: predicts climate, ocean-chemistry and oxygen feedbacks before deployment.

buildSteps.title: Choose a chassis
buildSteps.detail: Select a fast-growing, widely tolerant marine microbe already adapted to open-ocean conditions rather than inventing one from scratch.

buildSteps.title: Identify genetic targets
buildSteps.detail: Map the pathways that limit carbon fixation, growth rate, cell density and nutrient scavenging, so edits aim at bottlenecks rather than guesses.

buildSteps.title: Edit the genome
buildSteps.detail: Use gene-editing tools to install and tune those changes, then iterate through design–build–test cycles in the lab to measure growth and carbon uptake.

buildSteps.title: Build biocontainment
buildSteps.detail: Add dependence on a nutrient that is rare in the wild and kill switches that trigger when the organism leaves its intended environment.

buildSteps.title: Test in enclosed systems
buildSteps.detail: Grow the strain in sealed bioreactors and then in large floating mesocosms — enclosed bags of seawater — to see how it behaves with a real plankton community.

buildSteps.title: Run small open trials
buildSteps.detail: Release a limited patch in a defined ocean area, tracking spread, nutrient drawdown and how much carbon actually sinks, alongside controls.

buildSteps.title: Verify carbon export
buildSteps.detail: Confirm that the biomass and its carbon reach depth and stay there, using sediment traps, floats and chemical tracers.

buildSteps.title: Model and govern before scaling
buildSteps.detail: Only after verified export, containment performance and agreed international rules would any regional deployment be considered.

prerequisites.tech: Precise genome editing and synthetic biology
prerequisites.why: rewriting metabolic pathways in microbes is routine in the lab, though not yet at environmental scale.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of the ocean carbon cycle
prerequisites.why: how much carbon from surface blooms truly reaches the deep sea remains uncertain, which makes verification hard.
the limiting nutrients for ocean photosynthesis — iron, nitrogen, phosphorus — would have to be delivered in enormous quantities.
no engineered organism has been shown to stay contained in an open ecosystem at planetary scale.
carbon removal only has value if it can be measured credibly and independently.
there is no agreed framework for deliberate, large-scale modification of shared oceans and atmosphere.

pathway.milestone: lab and pilot-scale engineered algae for carbon capture, plus enclosed mesocosm experiments
pathway.unlocks: evidence on growth rates, carbon uptake and containment performance.

pathway.milestone: small, tightly monitored open-ocean trials with independent verification
pathway.unlocks: real numbers on how much carbon sinks and what happens to plankton communities.

pathway.milestone: agreed international rules, shared measurement standards and a decade of field data
pathway.unlocks: a legitimate basis for deciding whether regional deployment is acceptable.

pathway.milestone: carefully bounded regional deployments, if verified
pathway.unlocks: a measurable carbon-removal contribution alongside emissions cuts, not instead of them.

pathway.milestone: large-scale atmospheric tuning via engineered flora
pathway.unlocks: nothing reliable — the ecological and climate feedbacks are too poorly understood to promise.
